newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - YPF up in heavy New York trade.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - YPF up in heavy New York trade.

text.p: Argentine oil company YPF rose in heavy New York trade on Wednesday as investors returned to Latin American bellwether stocks.
YPF rose one to 26-7/8 in heavy mid-morning trade. The company was among the most actively traded on the New York Stock Exchange, with 1.3 million shares switching hands.

Ray Kelly, Latin American director at Robert Fleming, said high-profile Latin American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) such as YPF and Brazilian telecom Telebras were benefiting from rebalancing in global portfolios at the start of the year.
"Latin American is seeing a fair share of that money," he said. Argentina and Brazil in particular were getting greater attention because of improved political and economic fundamentals.
"The markets are looking a lot better than even (at the start of) 1996," he said.
Among other ADRs, Finnish telecom group Nokia rose 2-1/8 to 61-3/4 after Smith Barney set a 12-month target price for the stock of $99.
Spanish telephone company Telefonica de Espana rose two to 74-1/4 after Spain's Argentaria raised its state in the firm.
Advancers led decliners 251 to 186 among an 807-ADR index. Volume was 33 million shares.
